17.text: GENERAL CONCLUSIONS. — In conclusion, I must repeat, in the first place,

18.text: that the Russianization of the Chukchee has made no progress at all during

19.text: the two centuries of Russian intercourse with the Chukchee. The Chukchee

20.text: kept the language, all their ways of living, and their religion. Even the few

21.text: families of the river Chukchee of the Middle Anadyr have not adopted the

22.text: Russian language. They have adopted the Russian chimney on their huts;

23.text: and under Russian influence there have sprung up among them riddles and

24.text: proverbs, partly translated from the Russian, and of a character different from

25.text: that of the other folk-lore of the Chukchee; and that is all.

26.text: As to the question of what was brought into the life of the Chukchee

27.text: through Russian influence, I should say that the first thing brought by the

28.text: Russians was a request for tribute and war. The fate of the Chukchee, how-

29.text: ever, was different from the fate of all other native tribes, in that they success-

30.text: fully repelled the first, and held their ground in the second; and, when the

31.text: war at last ceased, they preserved intact all their national vigor, and so they

32.text: could avail themselves of peace. This explains the spread of the Reindeer

33.text: Chukchee westward and southward, and the subsequent increase of their herds.

34.text: In modern times, the same as two centuries ago, Russianization for this

35.text: nomadic and primitive people would mean destruction and death. It is their

36.text: good fortune that the latest contrivances of the Russian Administration, like

37.text: the “clans” and the “chiefs,” and the voluntary tribute, are mere outward

38.text: forms, and do not produce much change in their material or special life.

39.text: Russian influence has brought to the Chukchee tools and instruments of

40.text: iron, flintlocks and powder, iron kettles, and hardware. These are real acqui-

41.text: sitions. Colored beads, and overcoats of gaudy calico, are also to be counted

42.text: among such acquisitions, since they satisfy the æsthetic sense much better than
